stimuli.title: Ovi, Hema, Charu, Farah, Jaya, Bina, Uma, Pia occupy eight flats on floors 1 (bottom) to 4 (top). Each floor has Flat A to the west of Flat B. Each flat has one resident. For ordering only, count Floor 1 A, Floor 1 B, Floor 2 A, Floor 2 B, and so on.
stimuli.body:

• Jaya occupies floor 2, flat B.
• Charu lives in Flat B.
• Bina and Uma occupy flats with different letters.
• The floor numbers of Bina and Uma differ by 2.
• Farah and Bina occupy flats with the same letter on different floors.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
rural savings credit = ni su pa
rural digital growth = mi lu su
savings digital secure = mi ni re
credit growth secure = lu re pa
rural savings secure = ni re su
What is the code for “growth”?
questions.explanation: Answer: lu. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: rural = su, savings = ni, credit = pa, digital = mi, growth = lu, secure = re.

questions.stem:
Statements: U > W > R < Q < X.
Conclusions: I. U ≥ R   II. U ≥ X.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:

questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem: E is the brother of F. F is the mother of G. B is the father of E and F. How is E related to G?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. E is the brother of G’s mother F. Therefore E is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: H is the mother of C. G is the daughter of C. D is the father of C. How is G related to D?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. D is a parent of C, and G is C’s daughter. Hence G is D’s grandchild.

questions.stem: C is the only daughter of D. D is the father of C. F is the son of C. H is the sister of D. How is D related to F?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. D is the father of C, and C is F’s mother. Thus D is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 114 km south, turns left and walks 195 km, then turns left and walks 10 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 221. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 104 km along the initial direction and 195 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(104² + 195²) = 221 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 31 km east, turns left and walks 28 km, then turns left and walks 10 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 35. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 21 km along the initial direction and 28 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(21² + 28²) = 35 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 166 km north, turns right and walks 270 km, then turns right and walks 22 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 306. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 144 km along the initial direction and 270 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(144² + 270²) = 306 km.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some tokens are bonds. All bonds are branches. No branches is a loans.
Conclusions:
I. Some tokens are branches.
II. Some bonds are loans.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few tokens are bonds. Some bonds are branches. All branches are loans.
Conclusions:
I. All tokens are loans.
II. No bonds is a loans.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: No tokens is a bonds. Some bonds are branches. All branches are loans.
Conclusions:
I. All tokens are loans.
II. Some loans are bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few tokens are bonds. All bonds are branches. No branches is a loans.
Conclusions:
I. Some tokens are not bonds.
II. No bonds is a loans.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem: In a queue of 39 candidates, a candidate is 16th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 20. New front rank = 16+4 = 20. Back rank = 39 − 20 + 1 = 20.

questions.stem: A container holds 140 litres of pure milk. 28 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 89.6. Each replacement retains 4/5 of the milk. Remaining milk = 140 × (4/5)².

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 20%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹2700. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)

questions.stem: A boat covers 76 km in still water in 4 hours. If the stream flows at 4 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 2 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 30. Still-water speed = 19 km/h. Upstream speed = 19 − 4. Distance = speed × 2.

questions.stem: The average weight of 14 people is 44 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 59. New total minus old total = (14+1)×(44+1) − 14×44 = 59.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹27000 earns ₹12150 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 35707.5. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 15%. Compound amount = 27000 × (1 + 15/100)².

questions.stem: [Table set] What is the total number in the approved category at A and C together?
questions.explanation: Answer: 2460. Derived data: A: first category 1500, second category 900; B: first category 540, second category 360; C: first category 960, second category 1280; D: first category 900, second category 1200; E: first category 720, second category 1080. 1500 + 960 = 2460.

questions.stem: [Table set] If 25% of the rejected category at E is transferred to the approved category there, what is the new size of the approved category at E?
questions.explanation: Answer: 990. Derived data: A: first category 1500, second category 900; B: first category 540, second category 360; C: first category 960, second category 1280; D: first category 900, second category 1200; E: first category 720, second category 1080. New first category = 720 + 25% of 1080.

questions.stem: [Table set] If the approved category at C increases by 20% and the rejected category there decreases by 10%, what is the new total?
questions.explanation: Answer: 2304. Derived data: A: first category 1500, second category 900; B: first category 540, second category 360; C: first category 960, second category 1280; D: first category 900, second category 1200; E: first category 720, second category 1080. 960 × 1.20 + 1280 × 0.90.

questions.stem: [Table set] What is the average number in the rejected category across A, C and E? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 1086.67. Derived data: A: first category 1500, second category 900; B: first category 540, second category 360; C: first category 960, second category 1280; D: first category 900, second category 1200; E: first category 720, second category 1080. (900 + 1280 + 1080) ÷ 3.

questions.stem: [Table set] The combined total at A and D is what percentage more or less than the total at C? Give the absolute percentage difference, rounded to two decimals.
questions.explanation: Answer: 100.89. Derived data: A: first category 1500, second category 900; B: first category 540, second category 360; C: first category 960, second category 1280; D: first category 900, second category 1200; E: first category 720, second category 1080. Percentage difference = |total(A)+total(D)−total(C)| ÷ total(C) × 100.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 7:3. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 9 months. A receives ₹109200 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?
questions.explanation: Answer: 144300. Profit ratio is 84:27. Each ratio unit = ₹1300. Total = 111 × 1300.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 13 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 39. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+13)/(x+13) = 3/2 gives x = 13. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: A 120 m train moving at 86.4 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 10.8 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 5.71. Relative speed = (86.4 − 10.8) ×5/18 = 21 m/s. Time = 120/21.

questions.stem: [Bar set] The business category at D is what percentage of the agricultural category at B? (Round to two decimal places.)

questions.stem: [Bar set] A new branch F has a total equal to the average total at A and E. Its categories are split in ratio 2:3. What is the number in its second category?
questions.explanation: Answer: 1158. Derived data: A: first category 1100, second category 660; B: first category 600, second category 900; C: first category 600, second category 900; D: first category 480, second category 720; E: first category 900, second category 1200. Average total = (total A + total E)/2. The second category is 3/5 of that average.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 34 and 51 hours. An outlet empties it in 68 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank. (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 29.14. Net rate = 1/34 + 1/51 − 1/68 = 7/204 tank/hour. Required time = 29.14 hours.
